lead: Montana plumbing is built for long, deep winters, long drives and lots of private wells. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Billings to Missoula.
risk: frozen water lines and pipes, well and septic systems, and hard water in many areas
risk_short: frozen pipes, wells and hard water
why: Montana winters bring long stretches below zero, and frost goes deep. Water lines, crawl-space pipes and vacant cabins freeze when the heat fails. Many Montana homes are far from town, so plumbers often travel long distances.
Rural homes rely on private wells and septic systems, and hard water is common in many areas. The Montana Board of Plumbers licenses plumbers statewide.
problems: Many areas east of the Divide
tips: Never let the heat drop low during a cold snap.
Insulate pipes in crawl spaces and on outside walls.
areas: Calls come from Billings, Missoula, Great Falls, Bozeman, Butte, Helena, Kalispell and rural Montana.

faq.q: How do I winterize a Montana cabin?
faq.a: Shut off the water, drain the pipes and water heater, and put RV antifreeze in drain traps and toilets. If you leave heat on, keep it at a safe level and add a temperature alarm. A plumber can do the full winterization.
